facts.fact: Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists Equiano as in service since 2023, landing at Melkbosstrand, South Africa, owned 100% by Google.

Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists SAT-3/WASC as in service since 2001, landing at Melkbosstrand, South Africa, run by a 36-operator consortium including Telkom SA.

Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists WACS as in service since 2012, landing at Yzerfontein, South Africa, run by a 14-member consortium including MTN, Telkom SA and Vodacom.
Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists ACE as in service since 2012 and extended to Cape Town, South Africa in 2021, led by Orange.
Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists EASSy as in service since 2010, landing at Mtunzini, South Africa, led by WIOCC with Telkom SA among the members.
Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists SEACOM (original) as in service since 2009, landing at Mtunzini, South Africa.

Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) lists six in-service cables landing in South Africa at different stations: Melkbosstrand (Equiano, SAT-3/WASC), Yzerfontein (WACS), Cape Town (ACE) and Mtunzini (EASSy, SEACOM).

facts.fact: Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) flags EASSy as open access and shows a largely African consortium led by WIOCC with 16+ members, including Telkom SA, landing at Mtunzini.
Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) flags SEACOM (original) as open access; it lands at Mtunzini, South Africa.
Data Landscapers cable factsheet (AI-compiled, published 2026-06-03) says Equiano, though sole-owned by Google, has capacity sold to customers, landing at Melkbosstrand.
